name: Setpoint optimisation (heating/cooling dead-band)
basis: Heating 21→20, cooling 24→25 (doc example). Widened dead-band within comfort agreement.

name: Reduce DHW demand (low-flow fittings)
basis: DHW demand −19.5%: shower fraction 65% (mid 60–70%) × low-flow volume reduction 30% (aerator/regulator standard). Within the doc's −10..−25% band.

name: Larger ASHP — full DHW off gas
basis: Gas DHW off (share 0), ASHP serves 100% at high-temp SCOP 2.9 (mid 2.8–3.0). The principal carbon measure (gas→electric).

name: Waste-water heat recovery (WWHR)
basis: Design note: DHW demand scalar 0.82 (shower 65% × HX effectiveness 45% × config factor 0.6 ≈ −18%). Modelled as demand-litres ×0.82 (55→45.1). SAME PATH as 1.1 — see cumulative caveat.

name: Reduce fan duty
basis: Bedroom extract flow 2208→1590 (−28%, per doc's 2292→1656 case). Fan power falls with the cube law → SFP scaled by (flow ratio)² (0.9→0.47) so fan energy ∝ flow³.

name: Automatic room shut-off (keycard/occupancy master switch)
basis: Room plug load −25% (mid of doc's −20..−30% when unoccupied). Equipment baseload 5.04→3.78 W/m² (net occupancy-weighted).

name: Exhaust air over ASHP (COP uplift)
basis: Design note: preheat-stage COP +0.4 absolute (3.0→3.4), applies to the ASHP preheat share of DHW (dhw[1], 48%). SAME PATH as 1.4 — see cumulative caveat.

name: VRF metering, commissioning & diagnostic health check
basis: Design note sensitivity band: none / central +0.4 / strong (managed 3.9). CENTRAL (+0.4 on in-service VRF heating SCOP + cooling EER, 3.0→3.4) is the stack member; none/strong stored as sensitivity. SAME PATH as 3.2 — 3.2 composes on the post-3.1 state.

name: Interlinked heat recovery — VRF→DHW
basis: Off-model (Class C): monthly-coincidence calc, 55% capture. Neither engine models inter-plant heat flows.

name: Solar PV
basis: Off-model (Class C): 50 kWp × 950 kWh/kWp = 47.5 MWh/yr, 85% self-consumption; EUI UNCHANGED by construction (CRREM gross-demand rule). Carbon valued on the declining grid pathway.

name: Fabric — glazing G-value (solar film)
basis: Glazing g 0.55→0.42 (nearest library construction double_low_e; u unchanged at 1.4 — film reduces g, not u; doc target g 0.40). Expected marginal/counterproductive here (cuts useful winter heat, raises cooling). Film life ~10–15y in reality but note maps fabric→30y.

name: VRF replacement (current-gen R-32 heat recovery)
basis: Heating/cooling consumption −20% (spec 15–25%), via rated-SCOP substitution derated to in-service: eff 3.0→3.75 (=3.0/0.8). CUMULATIVE: computed against the post-3.1 state (3.4→4.25) per the note's double-count guard. Plus Class C refrigerant carbon ≈4.7 tCO₂e/yr (offmodel).

name: Communal lighting + controls
basis: Whole-building lighting magnitude −15% (2.0→1.7 W/m²) representing communal LED + PIR occupancy sensing on the communal fraction. [15% is a stated assumption — communal share × PIR saving.]

name: Brise soleil (external solar shading)
basis: 0.5 m horizontal overhang on the SW/S/W-facing glazing → modelled as south + west facades of the 4-orientation box (North_Axis 42). Seasonally selective (cuts summer sun, admits winter).

name: MVHR replacing central electric heating + bathroom extract
basis: Bedroom extract → balanced MVHR 80% HR, SFP 1.8 (mid 1.5–2.0). Electric panel heating (heating[1], 5%) removed → VRF 100%. Note: net effect may be adverse (summer) — modelling decides.

name: Heat-recovery bypass setpoint
basis: NO clean static-engine representation — seasonal HRV bypass is a control the static engine does not expose (no seasonal-recovery field). Modelled effect ≈ 0; a near-free control with a small summer cooling benefit not captured. Cost within 6.1.

name: Room load monitoring (sample sub-metering)
basis: Enabling: no demand change; converts assumed room load into data. Sizes 4.2.

name: Equipment efficiency at replacement
basis: £0 capex by definition (efficient spec at natural replacement). No energy claim modelled.

name: Kitchen/catering review + circuit metering
basis: Enabling: quantum unknown by design; no modelled demand change.

name: Building sub-metering package (plant + water)
basis: THE enabling measure: no demand change; resolves the report's largest unknown. First action overall.

name: Communal ventilation run-hours
basis: Within the 6.1 controls visit. Align HRV schedules to space use; small saving not separately modelled (within 6.1 / not a headline claim).

name: BMS setpoint realignment + schedules (consolidated controls visit)
basis: Cost-carrier for the settings measures (3.3, 5.4, 2.3). Their energy savings are claimed under those refs; 6.1 carries the £3,000 visit so the settings measures read £0 capex (avoids double-count).
